'''Peter Mann Winkler''' is a research mathematician, author of books on [[mathematical puzzles]] and of more than 130 research papers in mathematics<ref>[http://www.math.dartmouth.edu/~pw/papers/pubs.html Publication list] from Winkler's home page at Dartmouth.</ref> and patent holder in a broad range of applications, ranging from [[cryptography]] to marine [[navigation]].<ref name="pw">Information listed on [http://www.math.dartmouth.edu/~pw/ Peter Winkler's homepage] at Dartmouth.</ref> His research areas include [[discrete mathematics]], [[theory of computation]] and [[probability theory]].
He is currently the William Morrill Professor of Mathematics and Computer Science at [[Dartmouth College]].<ref>[https://math.dartmouth.edu/people/people-select.php?list=permanent Dartmouth mathematics faculty listing].</ref><ref>{{cite web | title=Peter Winkler | website=Simons Foundation | date=2019-10-11 | url=https://www.simonsfoundation.org/people/peter-winkler/ | access-date=2026-04-10}}</ref>

== Education and career ==

Peter Winkler studied mathematics at [[Harvard University]] and later received his PhD in 1975 from [[Yale University]] under the supervision of [[Angus Macintyre|Angus McIntyre]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=13141|name=Peter Winkler}}.</ref> He has also served as an assistant professor at [[Stanford]], full professor and chair at Emory and as a mathematics research director at [[Bell Labs]] and [[Lucent Technologies]].<ref name="pw"/> He was visiting professor at the [[Technische Universität Darmstadt]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.humboldt-foundation.de/pls/web/pub_hn_query.humboldtianer_details?p_externe_id=7000136161&p_lang=de&p_pattern=|title=Humboldt network profile of Peter Winkler|last=|first=|date=|website=www.humboldt-foundation.de|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2019-09-17}}</ref>

== Puzzle books ==

Winkler has published three books on [[mathematical puzzles]]:
* ''Mathematical Puzzles: A connoisseur's collection''<ref>Baylis, John. ''Mathematical Puzzles: A Connoisseur’s Collection'', by Peter Winkler. ''[[The Mathematical Gazette]]'' 90, no. 517 (2006): 186–88. http://www.jstor.org/stable/3621462</ref><ref>Gorini, Catherine A. ''Mathematical Puzzles: A Connoisseur’s Collection'', by Peter Winkler. ''[[The Mathematics Teacher]]'' 98, no. 5 (2004): 363–363. http://www.jstor.org/stable/27971734</ref> ([[A K Peters]], 2004, {{isbn|978-1-56881-201-4}}, translated to German and Russian)
* ''Mathematical Mind-Benders''<ref>Fischer, Joyce. ''Mathematical Mind-Benders'', by Peter Winkler. ''[[The Mathematics Teacher]]'' 102, no. 3 (2008): 238–39. http://www.jstor.org/stable/20876331</ref> (A K Peters, 2007, {{isbn|978-1-56881-336-3}})
* ''Mathematical Puzzles'' (A K Peters, 2021, {{isbn|978-0-36720-693-2}}).

Winkler is widely considered to be a pre eminent scholar in this domain. He was the Visiting Distinguished Chair for Public Dissemination of Mathematics at the [[National Museum of Mathematics]] (MoMath), gave topical talks at the [[Gathering 4 Gardner]] conferences, and wrote novel papers related to some of these puzzles.

== Bridge at the Enigma Club ==

Winkler's book ''Bridge at the Enigma Club''<ref>[https://www.bridgeworld.com/indexphp.php?page=/pages/bookstore/itemdetailpages/itemdetailpage_1689.html ''The Bridge World'' Bookstore] ''Bridge at the Enigma Club'' by Peter Winkler</ref> was a runner up for the 2011 [[Master Point Press]] Book Of The Year award.<ref>[http://bridge-tips.co.il/wp-content/uploads/2012/05/IBPA-Handbook.pdf The 2011 Master Point Press Book Of The Year Award] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201041220/http://bridge-tips.co.il/wp-content/uploads/2012/05/IBPA-Handbook.pdf |date=2017-12-01 }} 2014 IPBA Handbook, p. 176</ref>

== Recognition ==

In 2011, Winkler received the [[David P. Robbins Prize]] of the [[Mathematical Association of America]] as coauthor of one of two papers<ref>"Overhang", ''[[American Mathematical Monthly]]'', vol. 116, January 2009 ([https://arxiv.org/abs/0710.2357 Online]) <br>"Maximum Overhang", ''[[American Mathematical Monthly]]'', vol. 116, December 2009 ([https://arxiv.org/abs/0707.0093 Online])</ref> in the ''[[American Mathematical Monthly]]''.<ref>{{cite web | title=David P. Robbins Prize – Mathematical Association of America | website=Mathematical Association of America – Advancing the understanding of mathematics and its impact on our world | url=https://maa.org/david-p-robbins-prize/ | access-date=2026-04-10}}</ref>

== Paul Erdős anecdote ==

According to ''The Man Who Loved Only Numbers'', a biography of [[Paul Erdős]], he attended the [[bar mitzvah]] celebration for Peter Winkler's twins, and Winkler's mother-in-law tried to throw Erdős out:

{{blockquote|"Erdös came to my twins' bar mitzvah, notebook in hand," said Peter Winkler, a colleague of [[Ronald Graham|Graham]]'s at AT&T. "He also brought gifts for my children--he loved kids--and behaved himself very well. But my mother-in-law tried to throw him out. She thought he was some guy who wandered in off the street, in a rumpled suit, carrying a pad under his arm. It is entirely possible that he proved a theorem or two during the ceremony."<ref name="The Man Who Loved Only Numbers-CHAPTER-ONE">{{cite book 
 |url         = https://archive.org/details/manwholovedonlyn00hoff
 |title       = The Man Who Loved Only Numbers / The Story of Paul Erdös and the Search for Mathematical Truth
